how_it_wins:
Two commanders stand at opposite ends of one door. Brallin bills the table for every card that leaves your hand — each discard is 1 damage to EACH opponent and a +1/+1 counter. Shabraz pays you for every card that arrives — each draw is a +1/+1 counter and 1 life. A wheel is therefore two payments, and the 99 is the pile of cards that gets paid twice.

What has to be true is one thing. The engine declaration marks exactly one group `required`: a wheel. Nothing else in the deck starts itself. The goldfish (10,000 games, seed 42) reads a wheel drawn in 0.991 of games, 0.943 by turn six, mean turn 1.779. Both commanders are down by turn six in 0.834 of games.

The split the cards do not show is the most important thing here. The 99 holds 17 hand-refill effects and only NINE discard, so only nine pay Brallin: Anje's Ravager, Burning Inquiry, Jace's Archivist, Khorvath's Fury, Magus of the Wheel, Queen Kayla bin-Kroog, Reforge the Soul, Tolarian Winds, Windfall. Six shuffle the hand into the library (Echo of Eons, Time Reversal, Commit // Memory, Winds of Change, Molten Psyche, Whirlpool Warrior) and two put it on the bottom (Arjun, Teferi's Puzzle Box). Those eight refill you for the Shabraz half only, and refill the table with you. A discard wheel is drawn in 0.949 of games and 0.808 by turn six.

Two kills come off one ignition. The wheel kill — a discard wheel plus a stacked per-card damage source — assembles in 0.866 of games, 0.535 by turn six. The air kill — a wheel plus a flying body that grows on every card — 0.845 and 0.541.

What the table misreads: they see a draw deck and two 3/3s and rank you fourth. Stack 001 is the correction — one Windfall with both commanders out is 7 damage to each seat, 7 life to you, and two 10/10s. Say 7 per seat, never 21; 21 is the pod total and the two figures are not interchangeable.
mulligan:
Keep for the enabler, not the payoffs. You keep to a CLASS, not to a named card, and the class is a wheel.

All payoff and no wheel — four lands, Psychosis Crawler, Niv-Mizzet, Glint-Horn Buccaneer — is a ship: every one of those is a blank until a hand empties.

Prefer a DISCARD wheel. Burning Inquiry ({R}), Tolarian Winds ({1}{U}), Windfall ({2}{U}) and Reforge the Soul all pay Brallin. Winds of Change ({R}), Molten Psyche and Commit // Memory refill you and pay him nothing.

Shelter is not a keep on its own. {1}{W}, instant, protection from a colour and a card: the only card here that protects a creature at instant speed. Greaves and Boots need a turn and an equip first.

Lands: three. The goldfish keeps its first seven in 0.806 of games, but the diagnostic reads two stalled turns in a row in 0.1578 of games — worse than any tracked deck — and 6,659 of 7,937 stalled turns were mana-short, not hand-empty. You do not run out of cards. You run out of lands.

Read the lands, not the number. No basics in the 99, and only seven lands carry a basic type: Glittering Massif, Hallowed Fountain, Irrigated Farmland, Raugrin Triome, Sacred Foundry, Steam Vents, Thundering Falls. Without one of those down, Floodfarm Verge and Riverpyre Verge make W and R but not blue, and Nimbus Maze makes only colourless. Blue is what binds — 32 land sources against a 36 target, on-curve 0.785 counting only ungated lands — and Shabraz costs {3}{W}{U}. A two-lander of Floodfarm Verge and Nimbus Maze is a one-colour hand.

Gemstone Caverns upgrades a marginal six or seven when you are not on the play. It is a free land, and the card you exile is a Brallin trigger you were not going to get.

combo_lines.001:
This line turns on WHEN the fourteen triggers go on the stack. The discard and the draw are one resolution of Windfall; no player receives priority inside it. So all seven Brallin triggers and all seven Shabraz triggers wait, and Brallin is a 3/3 with no counters the whole time — through the discard AND through all seven draws. Only when Windfall has finished resolving and gone to the graveyard do the fourteen go on the stack together.

What it proves: Brallin triggers once per CARD you discard, seven times for seven cards. Each trigger is 1 damage to EACH opponent, so the total is 7 per seat and 21 across the pod. It also proves the counter count: one counter per resolution, so seven resolutions make Brallin a 10/10 and Shabraz a 10/10 flier, and you gain 7.

What it does not prove: nothing about a second damage source; that is stack 004. Note which cards did nothing. Rielle and Library of Leng were in the hand being discarded, not on the battlefield, so neither functioned: no extra draw, no card kept on top. Cast the wheel with the tollbooths already down.
combo_lines.002:
This line turns on one word: whether a discard redirected somewhere other than the graveyard is still a discard. It is. Library of Leng changes where the card goes, not whether the discard happened, so all four cards still count and Brallin still triggers four times — 4 per seat, 12 across the pod.

You bill the table for the cards and you do not lose them: the four go on top of your library in an order you choose, and Windfall's draw takes them straight back.

Read the draw count carefully, because it is not your discard count. Windfall draws everyone cards equal to the GREATEST number any single player discarded. So you draw your four back plus one card from beneath them. The corollary bites the other way: when you are the player with the biggest hand, you set the number for the table, and a full grip feeds three opponents seven cards each.

What it does not prove: Shabraz is off the board in this scenario, so the draw half is unpriced here. And the Leng trick has a hole stack 003 finds.
combo_lines.003:
This line turns on the difference between a cost and an effect, and it is the hole in the Library of Leng trick. Leng reads 'if an EFFECT causes you to discard a card'. A cycling cost's discard is paid during activation — no spell or ability resolved, so there is no effect, so Leng never applies. Raugrin Triome is in the graveyard and you cannot put it back on top.

Brallin does not care. His trigger condition is just 'you discard a card', and a cost payment is a discard: he triggers, and his trigger goes on the stack ABOVE the cycling ability, so the damage resolves BEFORE you draw. One counter, 1 damage per seat, 3 across the pod, then the draw.

Cycling is your instant-speed access to Brallin when you have no wheel, and nine cards in the 99 cycle — among them Shark Typhoon, Magmakin Artillerist, Nimble Obstructionist, Decree of Silence, Ominous Seas and three of the lands. If a seat is at 1, cycle in response and they are dead before the card is drawn.

What it does not prove: Shabraz is off the board here, so whether the cycle's draw also pays her is untested.
combo_lines.004:
This line turns on per-CARD against per-EVENT. Artist's Talent at level 3 replaces each noncombat damage event your sources deal with that damage plus 2.

Brallin's seven triggers are seven separate events. Each becomes 1 + 2 = 3, so seven resolutions deal 21 to each seat. Magmakin Artillerist's is ONE trigger — 'whenever you discard one or more cards' fires once per discard event, not once per card — so its 7 becomes 7 + 2 = 9, once. Total 30 per seat, 90 across the pod, three opponents from 40 to 10 off a single seven-card wheel.

Glint-Horn Buccaneer bills per card like Brallin; Magmakin bills per wheel. They are the same card until the Talent is at level 3, and then they are not.

Two more facts from the same line. The +2 is dealt by Brallin or by Magmakin, never by Artist's Talent, which deals zero damage all line. And Brallin's counters are unaffected: one per resolution, seven, 10/10.

What it does not prove: the Talent is stipulated at level 3 from an earlier turn. Getting there is {1}{R} then {2}{R} then {2}{R}, and only the last level does this.

threat_assessment:
No games are logged. Nothing below is table experience — it is a model and one simulation, and the simulation needs reading carefully.

THE FORGE RECORD, HONESTLY. 120 games against the standard-v3 pod returned 13 wins of 105 decided — 0.124, interval [0.074, 0.200] — last of four, behind sythis-enchantress 0.505, abaddon 0.276 and jarad-graveyard 0.095. The seat's own `engine_casts` says the engine never ran: Windfall 0 casts and 6 discards, Jace's Archivist 0 and 7. And that seat carries decklist_sha256 6a639725 — v0.1.0, the build, not the 2ca70e24 you sleeve. A newer 120-game run on the sleeved list was killed partway and reproduced the same failure: Faithless Looting discarded 16 times, cast zero. The AI will not empty its own hand, so no Forge figure for this deck is a verdict — and none is absent either.

WHEN YOU STOP BEING IGNORED. Three signals. The counters: the pair carry 6.745 by turn six and 38.377 by turn ten. The second body: both are down by turn six in 0.834 of games. The second damage source: Glint-Horn Buccaneer or Magmakin Artillerist turns one wheel into two bills, and a table that has seen Artist's Talent reach level 3 has seen stack 004 — 30 a seat.

WHAT TO DO ABOUT IT. Sequence the wheel last. Put the tollbooths down on quiet turns and pay them all at once; a wheel in your graveyard is the moment the table starts reading you as a draw engine.

COUNT THEIR MANA BEFORE YOU FIRE. Assume a blue seat with three or more open holds a counter and a white seat with four holds a sweeper. KEEPING A 3/3 ON THE TABLE is four cards against a 5–7 target: Lightning Greaves, Swiftfoot Boots, Kefnet the Mindful and Shelter. The goldfish prices only the two Equipment — drawn in 0.659 of games, 0.341 by turn six, the lowest by-turn-six rate of the twelve declared groups. Interaction is in hand in 0.525 of games at turn six and castable in 0.069.

Shelter is the only card here that protects a creature at instant speed: {1}{W} at instant speed, protection from the colour of your choice, and a card — which Shabraz turns into a counter and a life, so the protection part pays for some of itself. It beats a targeted coloured removal spell. It does not beat a wrath or colourless removal.

Know what you cannot do. deck-audit reads interaction-breadth at ZERO classes answered against a target of five — artifact, creature, enchantment, graveyard and land all uncovered. Against a problem permanent that has resolved, this deck's answer is usually to win first.
matchups:
ENCHANTMENT VALUE / CONTROL (the Sythis shape). The pod's best seat at 0.505, and it eliminated this deck 45 times, against 18 and 12 for the other two seats. It wins long, so do not play long. The unopposed goldfish kills by turn seven in 0.63 and by turn eight in 0.888; that is your window and it closes. Rhystic Study and Smothering Tithe are the two cards that tax a value deck without asking you to interact.

GRAVEYARD MIDRANGE (the Jarad shape). This is the matchup where your own engine works against you, and the fix is picking a different wheel. Nine of your 17 refills put four to seven cards into each player's graveyard, which is what they want. The six shufflers — Echo of Eons, Time Reversal, Commit // Memory, Winds of Change, Molten Psyche, Whirlpool Warrior — put hands into libraries instead, and Echo of Eons and Time Reversal shuffle GRAVEYARDS in too. Against a graveyard deck they are removal. They pay Brallin nothing: you trade your damage half for their engine.

CONTROL AND COUNTERSPELLS. Exactly two cards in the 99 walk through a counter: Nezahal, Primal Tide and Niv-Mizzet, Parun both read 'this spell can't be countered'. Nimble Obstructionist is not the answer it looks like: it counters an activated or triggered ability only, never a Swords to Plowshares and never a wrath. Decree of Silence cycles for {4}{U}{U} and counters a spell. Hold Shelter for the removal, not the counter: {1}{W} at instant speed is what keeps a commander through a targeted coloured spell.

GO-WIDE AND TOKEN DECKS. The worst class for the 99 as built. There are zero sweepers in the deck, and the audit's oracle-text heuristic now finds ZERO answered permanent classes of five — artifact, creature, enchantment, graveyard and land all uncovered — and calls that a floor. Brallin's damage hits players, not creatures, so a wide board does not shrink. Race it in the air: Shabraz flies. Plus The Locust God, Shark Typhoon, Improbable Alliance and Drake Haven, all of which make fliers off cards moving.

ANYTHING WITH A HAND-SIZE OR DRAW REPLACEMENT. Stated as an assumption, not a measurement: a seat with an opposing draw-replacement effect turns your wheel into their card advantage, and a seat with a discard tax turns it into nothing. Your own hand-size relief — Library of Leng, Reliquary Tower, Nezahal — is a three-card group drawn in 0.777 of games and 0.468 by turn six. Leng is the one that does double duty: stack 002 proves it keeps the cards AND bills the table.
